To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the next generation of added value mobile applications should be able to provide services to mobile people in the context area they are in and that this can be done through wireless context area networks.
the notion of context areas is a very powerful one to enable the next generation of added value mobile applications, and that context areas can be used for a ubiquitous access to information.
the next generation of mobile applications should provide added value to users through the support for the networking of individuals in the same physical or logical context area to form communities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a framework, which allows for the development of mobile applications that are able to provide added value services to mobile people, who are in the same physical or logical context area, and who are willing to communicate with each other.
the development of mobile and ubiquitous applications for the support of mobile people in the context area they are in.

(i) how to enable mobile and ubiquitous applications to provide added value for mobile users, (ii) how to enable the formation of communities in physical proximity or in the same logical context area, (iii) how to enable communication and information access in these communities and (iv) how to provide a seamless information access for mobile people in different context areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the next generation of added value mobile applications will provide the following services: (1) support for communication, (2) support for information access and (3) support for the creation of communities in the same context areas, where a context is constrained physically or logically.
mobile people are not only enabled to communicate and access information but that they can be supported to form communities in physical and logical context areas.
the next generation of mobile applications will enable mobile people to be part of communities, where the communities are built of people who are in the same context areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we envision a ubiquitous information access, where the context of a user is used as a filter for information access and where communities of users, who share the same context, are supported.

we try to address the problem of how to provide mobile people (i) with services that are specific for the current context they are in and (ii) how to provide mobile users with a way to form communities, where they can exchange information with other mobile people.
this paper tries to answer the question of how we can enable communities in physical and logical context areas as added value of mobile and ubiquitous applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to provide mobile people in the same WCAN with a common information space, that is accessible from their mobile devices, where the information space is tailored to the context area.
mobile people can be supported by applications in a very specific manner by providing services that are tailored to the context area they are currently in.
we are not only able to identify the added value of mobile applications for people, but also that the concept of communities can be used for a ubiquitous information access in the future.
